title: South Carolina AI Laws

reading.body:
South Carolina's only AI-related law is a ceremonial resolution, not a binding rule. H5085 declares March 30 to April 2, 2026, as AI Week and encourages citizens to learn about artificial intelligence.

That is the whole of the state's tracked AI legislation. The law creates no obligations for developers, deployers, or state agencies, and it sets no standards for how AI systems are built or used. For AI specifically, it means South Carolina currently imposes nothing on the compute, data centers, or power arrangements that AI depends on.

The data covers enacted laws only, read from enrolled text. It does not show pending bills, failed bills, or executive actions, so it cannot say whether South Carolina is moving toward regulation. It also does not measure enforcement, because there is nothing here to enforce.

How this page is kept
